rationale: Both are good refactors. Each removes the goroutines, the bubble sort and the recursive validation hack, adds named sentinel errors and a refactoring log, and sorts a copy of the input. A is easier to read. It relies on fmt width verbs (%-10s, %-25s, %13s) for column layout, so the header and each row are one line apiece. Its helpers are small and well named: less, validateDate, formatDate, formatDescription, formatAmount and groupThousands. B has nice touches: width constants, date layouts stored in the locale table, and stricter date validation with time.Parse. But its padRight helper is misnamed, since it returns only the padding and every call has to be written as x + padRight(x, w). The header is then built from nine WriteString calls. Its currencySymbol helper also quietly defaults to "$". A puts locale branching inside formatDate and formatAmount instead of the table, and writes WriteString(Sprintf) where Fprintf would be more idiomatic, but overall it is the clearer, simpler result.
